commit.message:
fix(browser): rollover tab-leak reclaim + hydrating-composer wait (D-C7)

Live defect chain (2026-09-19, fleet 35465340423.1): every failed #rollover()
leaked its NEW_TAB at the preconversation root forever. Combined with the D-C5
fresh-tab re-request the registry hit the 32-tab wall — live evidence:
total_at_wall=true, capacity_backpressure TAB_CAPACITY_EXCEEDED_PRE_EFFECT,
keepalive frozen at cycle_seq 1185, rollover_reason escalating
TYPE_EFFECT_AMBIGUOUS -> supervisor_composer_not_unique -> tab_capacity_exceeded.

- Leaked-rollover-tab ledger (#rolloverLeakedTabIds) with close-by-proof
  reclaim: registry-exists, not selected, not fleet-bound, not the keepalive
  tab, CAPTURE still at the preconversation ROOT. A tab that drifted to a
  conversation URL is never closed (the ambiguous send may have landed;
  reconciliation owns that surface).
- Drain points: top of #rollover() (before any NEW_TAB) and opportunistic in
  the ROLLOVER_AMBIGUOUS no-progress branch; bounded 3 closes per drain.
  Wedged CLOSE_TAB stays in the ledger and is retried — the retry loop is
  tab-neutral.
- D-C5 escape now reclaims the superseded attempt tab by proof and records
  reclaimed_tab_id in the recovery diagnostic.
- #typeAndSend composer wait: a fresh root tab hydrates asynchronously (first
  CAPTURE transiently shows zero/Several textboxes); bounded recapture
  (4 x 1.2s) before declaring supervisor_composer_not_unique. Healthy
  conversation tabs resolve on the first capture and never pay the wait.

Tests: rollover-tab-leak-reclaim.test.mjs (5) — same-cycle/next-cycle reclaim,
wedged-close retry ordering (drain BEFORE the next NEW_TAB), composer-wait
rescue, conversation-drift never closed, selected/fleet/keepalive obligations.
Full suite: 2465 tests, 2463 pass, 0 fail, 2 Windows-only skips. npm run check clean.
